summary: John's 6th-great-grandfather; Palatine immigrant from Jettenbach (ship Phoenix, 1754) who farmed beside the Delaware just north of Easton, near today's Lafayette College.
bio: Johann Andreas Grub was born at Jettenbach in the Duchy of Palatinate-Zweibrücken (Kusel district) in 1727, son of Johann Nickel Grub and Elisabeth Margaretha Lampert; WikiTree gives born 12 Sep, baptized 21 Sep 1727 (FamilySearch QPKL-RZNB, Reichenbach parish), his gravestone reads 12 Dec 1727, and GEDBAS gives 12 Jul 1727 (conflict; the tree shows 1727-1792). WikiTree flags a cousin of the same name as a possible confusion. He married Maria Elisabetha Christmann at Jettenbach on 19 Sep 1752. He was probably the 'Anderas Groh / Andreas Grub' on the ship Phoenix at Philadelphia, 1 Oct 1754 (Strassburger List 222); a 'Johannes Young/Jung' heads the same list. He appears in the Williams Twp congregation (1759), Bethlehem Twp tax list (1772), St. John's Lutheran, Easton (1773), and Forks Twp by 1781, with 100 acres in 1788; his tract adjoined the Delaware just north of colonial Easton, near today's Lafayette College campus. He died in Forks Twp on 6 Aug 1792 and was buried at St. John's Lutheran Cemetery, Easton (Find a Grave 28284890). His will of 11 Nov 1791 (Northampton Co. Register of Wills file #1430) names wife Mary Elizabeth and children Philip; Catherine (m. Gottlieb Hipp); Mary (m. George Stacher); Elizabeth (m. Peter Michael); John; Frederick; and Andrew; the widow and son Frederick were executors. An 'Andrew Grub' of the Northampton militia received a Militia Loan debt certificate (#10,758) - not proof of service and possibly another man (speculative). No French and Indian War service was found. A different 'Andreas Grub and w. Catharina' baptized daughters in Williams Twp 1748-1751, before this Andreas arrived - a separate man not to be merged. His presumed brother Johann Peter Grub (1724-1802) came on the Windsor in 1753. The tree profile shows a sailing-ship image.
